In [[algebraic geometry]], the '''Mumford vanishing theorem''' proved by [[David Mumford|Mumford]]<ref>{{Citation | doi=10.2307/2373099 | last1=Mumford | first1=David | author1-link=David Mumford | title=Pathologies. III |mr=0217091 | year=1967 | journal=[[American Journal of Mathematics]] | issn=0002-9327 | volume=89 | pages=94–104 | issue=1 | jstor=2373099| url=http://nrs.harvard.edu/urn-3:HUL.InstRepos:3597248 | url-access=subscription }}</ref> in 1967 states that if ''L'' is a semi-ample [[invertible sheaf]] with [[Iitaka dimension]] at least 2 on a [[complex projective manifold]], then

:<math>H^i(X,L^{-1})=0\text{ for }i = 0,1.\ </math>

The Mumford vanishing theorem is related to the [[Ramanujam vanishing theorem]], and is generalized by the [[Kawamata–Viehweg vanishing theorem]].
